Al-Zamakhshari kept faithful to his principle of not following a previous prophet, and thus failed in deriving from his other principle the obligation of worship by reason. The truth is that the Prophet ﷺ used to worship before the revelation and would devote himself to worship in the cave of Hira. If the phrase "I worship" came in the present tense, because in the past this specific worship that is meant in the verse did not occur, then the matter in it, and Allah knows best, is to be understood as the totality of the specific acts of worship that were not known except through revelation, not merely the affirmation of the unity of Allah and knowledge of Him, for that had always been established for him ﷺ before the commission, and Allah knows best. Or its coming in the imperfect is intended to depict his worship in the mind of the listener and to establish it in his understanding, like His saying: "Have you not seen that Allah sends down water from the sky, and the earth becomes green?" The original would be "fa-asbahat," but it was changed from that for the stated meaning, and this is a good view, so consider it, and Allah knows best.]] in it, meaning: you have not known me to worship an idol in the Jahiliyya, so how could it be expected of me in Islam?

﴿Wa lā antum ʿābidūna mā aʿbud﴾ (Nor are you worshippers of what I worship): that is, you have not worshipped at any time what I am upon the worship of.

If you say: Why was it not said "mā ʿabadt" (what I have worshipped), as it was said "mā ʿabadtum" (what you have worshipped)? I say: Because they used to worship idols before the mission, and he did not worship Allah the Exalted at that time. If you say: Why was "mā" used rather than "man" (who)? I say: Because what is meant is the attribute, as if he said: "I do not worship falsehood, and you do not worship the truth." It is also said that "mā" is verbal-masdariyya, meaning: "I do not worship your worship, and you do not worship my worship."

﴿Lakum dīnukum wa liya dīn﴾ (For you is your religion, and for me is my religion): your polytheism for you, and my monotheism for me. The meaning is: I am a prophet sent to you to call you to the truth and salvation, so if you do not accept from me and do not follow me, then leave me to my own, and do not invite me to polytheism.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever recites Surah al-Kafirun, it is as if he has recited a quarter of the Qur'an, and the rebellious devils will keep far from him, and he will be cleared of polytheism and protected from the greatest terror."

[Narrated by al-Tha'labi, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Wahidi with their chains to Ubayy ibn Ka'b. I say: its beginning was narrated by al-Tirmidhi.

Hadith of Anas, may Allah be pleased with him.]
